characters: Dzifa: a fourteen-year-old JHS 3 coder sketching neat flowchart symbols in her Computing jotter.
Sugri: her classmate assembling a 5-volt microcontroller, soil-moisture sensor, and LED indicator circuit.
Kweku: their classmate measuring the radius and height of a blue cylindrical water-storage drum with a tape measure.
Sir Acheampong: the JHS Computing and Robotics club patron.

narrationPlan.voice: Enthusiastic, analytical teen voices for Dzifa, Sugri, and Kweku; supportive Computing mentor voice for Sir Acheampong
narrationPlan.pace: Inventive, logical, and crystal-clear (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with distinct, natural voices for each JHS student and teacher.
Pause for two seconds at each comprehension check so learners can calculate or reason first.
Pronounce spreadsheet formulas, geometric terms, and security acronyms clearly and unhurriedly.

music: Playful marimba ostinato layered with crisp electronic synth plucks evoking smart African innovation (placeholder)
culturalNotes: Proposed NaCCA CCP curriculum links: Computing (B8.4.1.1 Programming, B8.4.2.1 Algorithms & Flowcharts, B8.4.3.1 Robotics), Career Technology (B8.4.1.2 Electronics, B8.3.3.1 PVC Pipes), and Mathematics (B8.3.2.2 Cylinder Volume, B8.4.1.1 Median & Outliers).
BECE Exam Precision: Reinforces standard flowchart geometry, LED series resistors, converting cm³ to litres (÷ 1,000), and choosing median when outliers are present.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated JHS age band (Basic 7 to Basic 9) and BECE conceptual level?
Are all mathematical calculations, Career Technology safety rules, and Computing syntax 100% accurate?
Verify cylinder calculation: (22/7) × 20² × 70 = 88,000 cm³ = 88 L, and remaining water 88 − 36 = 52 L.

teacherGuide.overview: Brings NaCCA Computational Thinking and Robotics alive in a Ghanaian school garden—combining flowchart logic, 5 V LED/sensor electronics, cylinder volume geometry, and statistical outlier handling.
learningGoals: Draw standard flowchart symbols (oval, parallelogram, rectangle, diamond) for selection loops.
Identify roles of sensors (input), microcontroller (brain), LED + resistor, and actuators (output).
Calculate cylindrical volume in cm³ and convert to litres (1,000 cm³ = 1 L).

beforeReading: Give learners five test scores: 50, 52, 52, 56, and 0 (absent). Ask them to compare mean (42) and median (52).
whileReading: Pause on Page 2 and ask learners to sketch the four flowchart shapes and label each meaning.
afterReading: Measure any cylindrical tin, cup, or Veronica bucket on campus and compute capacity in litres using V = πr²h.
discussion: Even without a physical robotics kit, how does flowchart thinking help us automate routines?
reflection: Why is drip irrigation directly to plant roots far wiser during Ghana’s dry season than spraying water across hot bare soil?

mathsExtension.task: After watering 36 litres out of the 88-litre cylindrical tank (radius r = 20 cm, π = 22/7), 52 litres (52,000 cm³) remain. Find the new height h of water in the drum to 1 decimal place.

support: Provide cut-out paper flowchart shapes (oval, parallelogram, diamond, rectangle) for groups to arrange on desks before drawing.
stretch: Write pseudocode using IF...THEN...ELSE and a WHILE loop matching Dzifa’s flowchart.

BECE Exam Precision: Reinforces standard flowchart geometry, LED series resistors, converting cm³ to litres (÷ 1,000), and choosing median when outliers are present.
localiseThis: Use safe 3 V–6 V battery holders or offline unplugged role-play if microcontrollers are not yet in the lab.
